title: Pulled Pork
subtitle: Slow-smoked American BBQ pork shoulder
excerpt: American low-and-slow BBQ pulled pork: a whole pork shoulder rubbed with spices and cooked for 12 to 14 hours over indirect heat or in the oven until the internal temperature reaches 95°C and the meat pulls apart in long, smoky, bark-edged shreds.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pulled pork is a cornerstone of American BBQ, particularly associated with the Carolinas (both North and South), where pigs were a primary food source from colonial times. The technique of low-and-slow cooking comes from the indigenous and African American traditions of cooking whole animals over smouldering wood for many hours. The cut is always pork shoulder (also called Boston butt in the US), which has the right fat content and connective tissue to break down over the long cook. The 'bark' (the crusty exterior from the Maillard reaction and rub caramelisation) is prized. Oven-braised pulled pork, while not true BBQ, produces good results without a smoker and is the most practical home method.

content.text: The target internal temperature is 95°C, not the safe-to-eat 65°C: only at 95°C has the collagen fully converted to gelatine and the meat will pull cleanly. Using an instant-read thermometer is essential. If slow-roasting in the oven, wrap tightly in foil after the first 2 hours to trap the moisture. Rest for at least 30 minutes before pulling.

Mix all the dry rub ingredients. Rub the mixture all over the pork, working it into the scored skin and any crevices. Leave uncovered in the refrigerator overnight for the deepest flavour, or at minimum 1 hour.

Heat the oven to 130°C / fan 110°C / gas 1. Place the pork skin-side up in a deep roasting tin. Add the cider vinegar and 100 ml water to the tin. Cover very tightly with foil. Roast for 6 to 7 hours, checking occasionally.

Remove the foil. Increase the heat to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6. Roast for a further 30 to 45 minutes until the skin is crispy and the internal temperature reads 95°C on an instant-read thermometer. Rest for 30 minutes. Remove the bone and pull the meat apart with two forks. Serve in brioche rolls with coleslaw.
